After several years building educational technology at Sizzle AI , I’m thrilled to share that we’ve been acquired by Campus – a two-year college reimagined for the next generation of students. From the moment I met Tade Oyerinde and the team, I was inspired by what they’ve built. Campus isn’t just another tech-driven education startup — it’s human-driven at its core. Every student is paired with a guidance counselor, teaching assistants, and inspiring professors from great universities. They get free tutoring, help navigating financial aid, and even a laptop to make sure nothing stands in the way of learning. I’m joining Campus as VP of Engineering, where I’ll be helping to bring together the effective, AI-driven learning tools we built at Sizzle with the human-first education Campus provides. Read more about the acquisition here: https://lnkd.in/eQh9JuwW If you’ve ever felt like tech has lost its soul and you want to build with purpose, helping make the world better through education, come join us. Hi everyone :) I don't normally post on LinkedIn, but I wanted to share an experience I had recently with a company I interviewed with through WaterlooWorks. In keeping this as factual as possible, I applied to a Cerebras co-op role that was advertised as having one open position. After my interview I received an informal offer, proceeded to decline another interview offer along with another external offer from another company, then later learned the one spot on WaterlooWorks went to someone else. That sequence caused a lot of wasted effort and stress. After having a conversation with the recruiter, I learned that the reason I did not ultimately receive the offer was because I did not commit fully to them upon receiving my informal offer. However, I had no idea the offer was conditional upon this, as this fact was not shared with me. In fact, it has repeatedly been encouraged by CECA, the co-op program itself, for students to weigh their options carefully before deciding on rankings. As a result, I was unable to receive a match through WaterlooWorks this cycle. I do feel upset, but ultimately, I’m sharing this so other students (especially those in Waterloo’s co-op program) know how critical it is to not assume that an informal offer is final. This experience highlighted for me how damaging miscommunication can be in co-op recruiting. I’m still seeking a Fall 2025 placement. If anyone knows of openings for a 3A Computer Science student skilled in the fields of linear algebra/robotics/computer vision/performance computing, I’d be grateful for any referrals. Meanwhile, I hope this helps other co-op students avoid similar confusion in the future. update: Hey everyone :) Thank you all so much for your responses, reactions, and taking the time out of your day in reading this post. I've honestly been blown away by the empathy and encouragement you have all shown to this post. As someone who rarely uses social media, making this post felt really overwhelming at first, but this experience has been incredibly validating, and I feel incredibly seen. Thank you all, from the bottom of my heart. 💛 ...more ...more
